name: affine
title: Learn an affine function
description: Your goal is to learn the relationship between x and y from the public examples below, then predict y for new values of x. The relationship is affine, meaning it has the form y = a * x + b for fixed, unknown coefficients a and b. Design a solution that generalises to new inputs and minimises its prediction error.
solution_interface: Write a self-contained final_solution.py with a function named predict(xs). The argument xs is a list of numbers. Return a Python list with one finite numeric prediction for each input, in the same order. The evaluator loads your file and calls predict(xs). For example, predict([0, 1]) must return a list containing two predictions.
metric_description: Fitness is the mean absolute error over the evaluation inputs. For each input, take the absolute difference between your prediction and the reference value, then average those differences. A fitness of zero means every prediction was correct on that evaluation set.
constraints: Use the public training examples to determine the relationship. Evaluation queries may include values outside the range of the training inputs.
Use Python and its standard library. Keep all code and fitted parameters needed for prediction in final_solution.py.
Return finite numbers. Boolean values, missing predictions, and extra predictions are invalid.
The solution must run independently of scratch.py, the experiment ledger, and any development files.
Use only the supplied task information. Access to private reference answers, evaluator internals, and network services is outside the solution interface.
evaluation: During development, use fitness-eval to measure the current solution on development queries. After development, the runner selects the best officially scored revision and evaluates it on a separate set of final queries. This task is deterministic, so its evaluator does not use the random seed.
scope: This synthetic task demonstrates the research workflow. Its results are intended to check that the workflow operates correctly.
